memories.author: D05
memories.text: GERD with heartburn and regurgitation. Chronic urticaria with daily wheals. Hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 50 mcg. Symptoms: retrosternal burning after meals, pruritic wheals especially evenings, fatigue, weight gain. Exam: BMI 28, mild epigastric tenderness, no lymphadenopathy, skin shows scattered erythematous wheals. Plan: start pantoprazole 40 mg OD before breakfast, domperidone 10 mg BD before meals, antacid gel SOS, levothyroxine 50 mcg OD, levocetirizine 5 mg OD. Order H. pylori stool antigen, CBC with eosinophils, TSH, free T4.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow-up appointment booked for 2025-07-10 at 10:00 with Dr Suresh Menon (D05).

memories.author: D05
memories.text: GERD: heartburn reduced to twice weekly. Urticaria: wheals persist despite levocetirizine, worse at night. Hypothyroidism: fatigue improved slightly. Exam: no abdominal tenderness, skin shows scattered wheals, no thyroid enlargement. Spirometry: FEV1 2.85 L (92% pred), FVC 3.40 L (88%), FEV1/FVC 0.84 (no change). Asthma Control Test not applicable. Plan: increase levothyroxine to 75 mcg OD, add cetirizine 10 mg HS, continue pantoprazole and domperidone, levocetirizine OD.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Via clinic app: 'Doctor, my hives have flared again over the past week, especially after eating out. I missed my evening cetirizine a couple of times. Also feeling some throat burn after spicy meals.'

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Chest X-ray (PA): lungs clear, no infiltrate or pleural effusion. Cardiac silhouette normal. No evidence of pneumonia or malignancy. Mild hiatal shadow suggestive of hiatus hernia.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: GERD: symptoms controlled on current regimen, occasional heartburn after heavy meals. Urticaria: daily wheals, some angio‑edema of lips, poorly controlled despite dual antihistamines. Hypothyroidism: euthyroid on levothyroxine 75 mcg. Exam: BMI 27.5, no thyroid nodule, skin shows widespread wheals with occasional lip swelling. Plan: refer to dermatology for chronic urticaria evaluation, continue current meds, consider step‑down pantoprazole if GERD stays stable.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Referral to Dermatology, Bangalore Medical Centre for evaluation of chronic urticaria inadequately responding to high‑dose second‑generation antihistamines. Request assessment for possible autoimmune urticaria and consideration of omalizumab.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Dermatology review: chronic spontaneous urticaria, autologous serum skin test positive. Recommend continuing levocetirizine 10 mg OD and cetirizine 10 mg HS, add low‑dose prednisolone 5 mg alternate days for 2 weeks, consider omalizumab if refractory. No immediate need for adrenal suppression.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: GERD: heartburn absent for 4 weeks, no regurgitation. Tolerating reduced pantoprazole. Urticaria: wheal frequency down to 3‑4 days/week after dermatology advice, no angio‑edema. Hypothyroidism: stable on levothyroxine 75 mcg. Exam: BMI 26.8, skin shows faint scattered wheals, no thyroid enlargement. Spirometry: FEV1 2.90 L (94% pred), FVC 3.45 L (90%), FEV1/FVC 0.84 (+0.05 L vs last). Plan: step down pantoprazole to 20 mg OD, continue domperidone PRS, levothyroxine 75 mcg, antihistamines as prescribed.
